newsitem.title: USA: Dlr closes broadly higher in US as mark, yen fade.
newsitem.headline: Dlr closes broadly higher in US as mark, yen fade.

text.p: The dollar ended sharply higher as U.S. investors extended overnight rallies against the mark and yen and also bought dollars against sterling.
The dollar gained on the mark overnight after European officials over the weekend formally set 990 as the mark/lira central rate in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).
Mark/lira traded just under 990 during the session before rebounding a bit to 993 in late U.S. trade.
Meanwhile, the dollar continued to climb versus the yen after a Japanese official hinted Japan's interest rates will remain at current historic lows.
"The dollar strengthened on the back of the decline in the mark against the lira," said John McCarthy, foreign exchange manager at ING Barings.
A report showing West German consumer inflation fell in November also hurt the mark by dampening expectations for higher interest rates in Germany, dealers said.
The dollar closed at 1.5233/38 marks, up from 1.5145/50 at the open and 1.5065/75 at Friday's close. The dollar closed at 112.62/65 yen, up from an open of 112.46/51 and 111.32/42 at Friday's close.
In Tokyo, Bank of Japan executive director Tadayo Honma warned a banking symposium that continued failures of Japanese financial institutions could not be ruled out.

This came less than a week after Japanese officials shuttered troubled Hanwa Bank and suggested Japan's economy was still too weak to allow an increase in the official discount rate from its meager 0.5 percent level.
Low Japanese and German interest rates enhance the relative value of higher-yielding U.S. assets denominated in dollars.

"The financial backdrop in the U.S. is pretty dollar supportive, while the focus in Japan is on the soft environment highlighted by the banking problem," said Lisa Finstrom, currency analyst at Smith Barney.
The dollar triggered stop/loss buying above 1.52 marks and 112 yen, but failed to break through resistance at 1.5260/70 marks, dealers said.
Sterling rose modestly in overnight trading, but later lost ground as investors took profits after a strong sterling rally in recent sessions, dealers said.

U.K. Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke denied reports that Britain would seek to informally link the pound to the proposed single European currency, insisting sterling would remain an independent unit.
But with Britain set to unveil its 1997-8 budget Tuesday, investors sold pounds to book profits in case the fiscal plan contains news that hurts the currency.
"Clarke's comments calmed everybody down, but obviously people are still very anxious about sterling," said Finstrom.
The British pound fell to $1.6681/86 from $1.6800/10.
The Swiss franc slipped on talk that Swiss pension funds are considering broadening their investment portfolios to include more foreign assets, dealers said.
"There was talk of a large investor buying dollars and marks against the Swiss franc," added Stephen Jury, chief foreign exchange dealer at Union Bank of Switzerland.
The dollar hit a 21-month high at 1.2905 Swiss francs before closing at 1.2880/90, up from 1.2770/80.
The dollar rose to Canadian $1.3428/33 from C$1.3397/02. The Australian dollar closed at $0.8100/05, down from $0.8123/28. -- Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664
